title: 聊天與表達想法
subtitle: Chatting: opinions, reactions and giving reasons

vocab.gloss: to believe; to think; to consider; to feel

example.hanzi: 我認為這家店的菜很好吃。
example.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè jiā diàn de cài hěn hǎochī.
example.gloss: I think the food at this restaurant is really good.

vocab.gloss: to be convinced (that sth is true); to believe; to accept sth as true

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn nǐ néng kǎo de hěn hǎo.
example.gloss: I believe you can do well on the exam.

example.hanzi: 其實我不太喜歡喝咖啡。
example.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ bú tài xǐhuān hē kāfēi.
example.gloss: Actually, I don't really like drinking coffee.

vocab.gloss: to think (i.e. to take it to be true that ...) (Usually there is an implication that the notion is mistaken – except when expressing one's own current opinion.)

example.hanzi: 我以為今天會下雨，其實沒有。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi jīntiān huì xià yǔ, qíshí méiyǒu.
example.gloss: I thought it would rain today, but actually it didn't.

vocab.gloss: to understand; to realize; to find out

example.pinyin: Wǒ bú tài liǎojiě tā de yìsi.
example.gloss: I don't quite understand what he means.

vocab.gloss: to speak; to explain; to negotiate

example.hanzi: 老師講得很慢，我都聽得懂。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiǎng de hěn màn, wǒ dōu tīng de dǒng.
example.gloss: The teacher speaks slowly, so I can understand it all.

grammar.title: 說出看法：認為 / 以為 / 相信
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 認為／以為／相信 + （一個句子）
grammar.explanation: To give an opinion, put a whole sentence after 認為, 以為 or 相信. 認為 = 'I think / in my view', used for an opinion you still hold. 以為 = 'I thought (but I was wrong)', used when what follows turns out not to be true; it is often followed by 其實… to say what is really the case. 相信 = 'I believe / I'm sure', used when you trust that something is or will be true. Note that you do not need 是 or 說 before the clause: 我認為這家店很貴。
grammar.contrast: 認為 vs 以為: both translate as 'think', but 以為 tells the listener the idea was mistaken. 我認為他會來 = I think he'll come (still my view); 我以為他會來 = I thought he'd come (he didn't). If you are stating your current opinion, always use 認為.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 我以為這本書很好 when they simply mean 'I think this book is good'. To a Taiwanese ear that says 'I used to think it was good — but it isn't.' Use 認為 (or 覺得) for a current opinion, and save 以為 for beliefs that turned out to be wrong.

examples.hanzi: 我認為騎腳踏車比搭捷運快。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi qí jiǎotàchē bǐ dā jiéyùn kuài.
examples.gloss: I think riding a bike is faster than taking the MRT.

examples.hanzi: 我以為你今天不來，其實你來了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ jīntiān bù lái, qíshí nǐ lái le.
examples.gloss: I thought you weren't coming today, but actually you came.

examples.hanzi: 我相信他講的話都是真的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn tā jiǎng de huà dōu shì zhēn de.
examples.gloss: I believe everything he says is true.

grammar.title: 其實：其實…（跟你想的不一樣）
grammar.explanation: 其實 'actually, in fact' comes at the start of the second clause, before the verb. It corrects or adds something the listener may not expect, and it very often follows a 以為 clause: 我以為…，其實…。
grammar.contrast: 真的 means 'really/truly' and stresses that something IS so; 其實 signals that the real situation is different from what was assumed. 這家店真的很貴 = it really is expensive; 其實這家店很貴 = actually (contrary to what you thought) it's expensive.
grammar.common_error: Learners put 其實 after the verb, like English 'I like it actually'. In Chinese 其實 goes before the subject or right after it — 其實我很喜歡, never 我很喜歡其實.

examples.hanzi: 他以為我生病了，其實我只是太累。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐwéi wǒ shēngbìng le, qíshí wǒ shì tài lèi.
examples.gloss: He thought I was sick; in fact I was just too tired.
Actually, you understand me very well.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 小明，你認為這家店的牛肉麵好吃嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Xiǎomíng, nǐ rènwéi zhè jiā diàn de niúròu miàn hǎochī ma?
dialogue.gloss: Xiaoming, do you think the beef noodles at this place are good?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 我認為很好吃，我每個週末都來吃。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi hěn hǎochī, wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu lái chī.
dialogue.gloss: I think they're great — I come and eat here every weekend.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 真的嗎？我以為你不喜歡吃麵。
dialogue.pinyin: Zhēn de ma? Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù xǐhuān chī miàn.
dialogue.gloss: Really? I thought you didn't like noodles.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 其實我最喜歡吃麵，你不太了解我。
dialogue.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ zuì xǐhuān chī miàn, nǐ bú tài liǎojiě wǒ.
dialogue.gloss: Actually, noodles are my favourite — you don't really know me.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 那你講講看，附近還有哪家好吃？
dialogue.pinyin: Nà nǐ jiǎngjiang kàn, fùjìn hái yǒu nǎ jiā hǎochī?
dialogue.gloss: Then tell me — what other good places are there nearby?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 我相信你吃了就知道，這家最好吧！
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn nǐ chī le jiù zhīdào, zhè jiā zuì hǎo ba!
dialogue.gloss: I'm sure once you eat you'll know — this one's the best!

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè jiàn yīfú hěn piàoliang.
sentences.gloss: I think this piece of clothing is very pretty.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn tā shuō de huà.
Lǎobǎn jiǎng de tài kuài le.

passage.title: 那家店
passage.hanzi: 昨天我和小明去學校附近吃飯。我以為那家店很貴，其實一個便當八十塊。小明說他常常來，老闆對客人很好，還會多給一點菜。我認為這家店的菜真的很好吃。回家的路上，小明和我講了很多他家裡的事，我也比以前了解他了。我相信下個週末我們還會再來。
passage.gloss: Yesterday Xiaoming and I went to eat near the school. I thought that place was expensive, but actually a lunchbox is only eighty dollars. Xiaoming said he comes often; the owner is nice to customers and even gives you a little extra food. I think the food there really is delicious. On the way home, Xiaoming told me a lot about his family, and I understand him better than before. I'm sure we'll come again next weekend.

vocab.gloss: interjection or grunt of agreement; uhm; Ah, OK

example.hanzi: 對啊，我也覺得這家店的麵很好吃。
example.pinyin: Duì a, wǒ yě juéde zhè jiā diàn de miàn hěn hǎochī.
example.gloss: Yeah, I also think the noodles at this place are really good.

vocab.gloss: heel; to follow closely; to go with

example.hanzi: 我週末想跟朋友去逛夜市。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò xiǎng gēn péngyǒu qù guàng yèshì.
example.gloss: I want to go to the night market with friends this weekend.

vocab.gloss: pertaining to; concerning; with regard to

example.hanzi: 關於這個問題，我們明天再說。
example.pinyin: Guānyú zhège wèntí, wǒmen míngtiān zài shuō.
example.gloss: As for this question, let's talk about it tomorrow.

example.hanzi: 別人的事情，你不要問太多。
example.pinyin: Biérén de shìqíng, nǐ búyào wèn tài duō.
example.gloss: Don't ask too much about other people's business.

vocab.gloss: other; (sth or sb) else; the rest

example.hanzi: 其他同學都已經回家了。
example.pinyin: Qítā tóngxué dōu yǐjīng huí jiā le.
example.gloss: All the other classmates have already gone home.

example.hanzi: 這個便當是我自己做的。
example.pinyin: Zhège biàndāng shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de.

grammar.title: 「跟」— doing something with someone / telling someone
grammar.pattern: Subject + 跟 + Person + Verb (一起做／說)
grammar.explanation: 跟 goes BEFORE the verb, not after it. 我跟他一起吃飯 = 'I eat with him'; 我跟他說 = 'I tell him / say to him'. 跟 can also simply link two nouns like 'and': 我跟我妹 (me and my sister). In Taiwan spoken Mandarin 跟 is the everyday choice for both uses.
grammar.contrast: 跟 vs 和: both can mean 'with/and', but 和 sounds more written and is used mostly to link nouns in lists, while 跟 is what people actually say out loud in Taiwan, especially before a verb (跟你說, 跟我去). 對 also appears with 說 (對我說), but it feels one-directional and more formal; if two people are talking, use 跟.
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and put the 'with' phrase after the verb: ✗ 我去看電影跟朋友. Chinese needs 跟 + person BEFORE the verb: ✓ 我跟朋友去看電影.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn lǎobǎn shuō le zhè jiàn shì.
examples.gloss: I told the boss about this.

examples.hanzi: 你要不要跟我們一起去逛夜市？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào bú yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ qù guàng yèshì?
examples.gloss: Do you want to go to the night market with us?

examples.hanzi: 這件事我不想跟別人說。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù xiǎng gēn biérén shuō.
examples.gloss: I don't want to tell other people about this.

grammar.title: 「關於」— bringing up a topic
grammar.explanation: 關於 introduces the topic you are about to talk about, and it normally sits at the front of the sentence, followed by a small pause: 關於那個工作，我還沒想好。It is very common when you change subject while chatting.
grammar.contrast: 關於 vs 對: 關於 marks a topic ('concerning X'), while 對 marks the target of an attitude (對這個工作很有興趣 → 'toward'). If you can say 'as for', use 關於.
grammar.common_error: Putting 關於 in the middle like English 'about': ✗ 我想說關於我自己. Say ✓ 關於我自己，我想說一點事情，or just use 說 + object: 我想說我自己的事。

examples.hanzi: 關於週末的事，我晚一點再跟你說。
examples.pinyin: Guānyú zhōumò de shì, wǒ wǎn yìdiǎn zài gēn nǐ shuō.
examples.gloss: As for the weekend plan, I'll tell you a bit later.

examples.hanzi: 關於這本書，其他人有什麼意思？
examples.pinyin: Guānyú zhè běn shū, qítā rén yǒu shénme yìsi?
examples.gloss: About this book, what do the others think?

examples.hanzi: 關於台北的捷運，我知道的不多。
examples.pinyin: Guānyú Táiběi de jiéyùn, wǒ zhīdào de bù duō.
examples.gloss: When it comes to the Taipei MRT, I don't know much.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ zài gēn shéi shuōhuà a?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 我跟我哥。他問我關於週末的事情。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ gēn wǒ gē. Tā wèn wǒ guānyú zhōumò de shìqíng.
dialogue.gloss: With my older brother. He's asking me about the weekend.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐmen zhōumò yào qù nǎlǐ wán?
dialogue.gloss: Where are you guys going this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 還沒想好。其他人想看電影，我自己想去逛夜市。
dialogue.pinyin: Hái méi xiǎng hǎo. Qítā rén xiǎng kàn diànyǐng, wǒ zìjǐ xiǎng qù guàng yèshì.
dialogue.gloss: Not decided yet. The others want to see a movie; I myself want to go to the night market.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 夜市好玩啊！別人怎麼說，你聽自己的就好。
dialogue.pinyin: Yèshì hǎowán a! Biérén zěnme shuō, nǐ tīng zìjǐ de jiù hǎo.
dialogue.gloss: The night market is fun! Whatever others say, just listen to yourself.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, nà wǒmen yìqǐ qù ba!

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ gēn wǒ mèimei yìqǐ kàn diànyǐng.
sentences.gloss: I watch a movie with my little sister.

sentences.pinyin: Guānyú zhōumò de shì, wǒ wǎn yìdiǎn zài gēn nǐ shuō.
sentences.gloss: As for the weekend, I'll tell you a bit later.

sentences.pinyin: Zhège biàndāng shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de.
Biérén de shìqíng, nǐ búyào wèn tài duō.
sentences.gloss: Don't ask too much about other people's business.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng chī qítā de dōngxi.
sentences.gloss: I don't want to eat anything else.

passage.title: 中午的話題
passage.hanzi: 我在台北上班，中午常跟同事一起吃便當。我們最愛說的話題是吃的東西：哪家店的牛肉麵好吃，哪家的珍珠奶茶最甜。有的人也喜歡說關於別人的事，我自己不太喜歡那樣。我覺得跟人說話，說自己知道的、喜歡的就好；其他的事，別人想說我再聽。
passage.gloss: I work in Taipei, and at noon I often eat a lunchbox with my coworkers. Our favorite topic is food: which shop has good beef noodles, whose bubble tea is the sweetest. Some people also like to talk about other people's affairs, but I don't really like that. I think when you chat with people, it's enough to talk about what you yourself know and like; as for other things, I'll listen if someone wants to bring them up.

example.hanzi: 你今天為什麼沒來上課？
example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān wèishénme méi lái shàngkè?
example.gloss: Why didn't you come to class today?

vocab.gloss: for; for the purpose of; in order to

example.hanzi: 為了考試，我每天晚上都讀書。
example.pinyin: Wèile kǎoshì, wǒ měi tiān wǎnshàng dōu dúshū.
example.gloss: For the exam, I study every evening.

vocab.gloss: if; in case; in the event that

example.hanzi: 如果明天下雨，我們就不去夜市了。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù yèshì le.
example.gloss: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go to the night market.

vocab.gloss: although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

example.hanzi: 這家店的麵雖然貴，可是真的好吃。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miàn suīrán guì, kěshì zhēn de hǎochī.
example.gloss: Although this shop's noodles are expensive, they're really tasty.

vocab.gloss: (not only ...) but also; moreover; in addition

example.hanzi: 他會說中文，而且說得很好。
example.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Zhōngwén, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
example.gloss: He can speak Chinese, and he speaks it well too.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiān xǐ shǒu, ránhòu chīfàn.
example.gloss: I wash my hands first, then eat.

grammar.title: 為了 (purpose) vs 因為 (reason)
grammar.pattern: 為了 + [purpose]，S + V ／ 因為 + [reason]，(所以) + [result]
grammar.explanation: 為了 tells you what someone is aiming at: it is followed by a noun or a verb phrase that is the goal, and the main clause says what they do to reach it. 因為 tells you why something happened: it is followed by a full reason clause, and is often paired with 所以 in the second half. Both start the first clause, but 為了 answers 'what for?' while 因為 answers 'why?'.
grammar.contrast: 因為 + [reason]，所以 + [result]. If the part after the connector is something you already know is true (I'm tired / it's raining), use 因為. If it is something you still want to get or achieve (to pass the exam / for my health), use 為了.
grammar.common_error: Learners put a whole reason clause after 為了, e.g. 為了我很忙，我沒去. That must be 因為我很忙，所以我沒去. 為了 can only be followed by the goal itself, not by a reason with a subject and a state verb.

examples.hanzi: 為了學中文，我來台灣了。
examples.pinyin: Wèile xué Zhōngwén, wǒ lái Táiwān le.
examples.gloss: I came to Taiwan in order to learn Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 為了身體好，他每天早上跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ hǎo, tā měi tiān zǎoshàng pǎobù.
examples.gloss: For his health, he runs every morning.

examples.hanzi: 因為天氣太熱，所以我們不出門。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi tiānqì tài rè, suǒyǐ wǒmen bù chūmén.
examples.gloss: Because the weather is too hot, we're not going out.

grammar.title: 先……然後……
grammar.explanation: Use 先 in the first clause and 然後 in the second to lay out two actions in order. 先 goes after the subject and before the verb; 然後 goes at the front of the second clause.
grammar.contrast: 而且 also joins two clauses, but it adds one more fact about the same thing (它很便宜，而且很好吃), not a next step in time.
grammar.common_error: Saying 我先吃飯，然後我先看電視 — 先 belongs only to the first action. Also don't put 先 before the subject (先我吃飯 is wrong).

examples.hanzi: 我們先去吃便當，然後去看電影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān qù chī biàndāng, ránhòu qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.gloss: Let's first go eat a lunch box, then go see a movie.

examples.hanzi: 她先搭捷運，然後騎腳踏車回家。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiān dā jiéyùn, ránhòu qí jiǎotàchē huí jiā.
examples.gloss: She takes the MRT first, then rides a bike home.

examples.hanzi: 你先寫名字，然後給我這張紙。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān xiě míngzì, ránhòu gěi wǒ zhè zhāng zhǐ.
examples.gloss: Write your name first, then give me this sheet of paper.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 你上個週末為什麼沒去夜市？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ shàng ge zhōumò wèishénme méi qù yèshì?
dialogue.gloss: Why didn't you go to the night market last weekend?

dialogue.speaker: 阿明
dialogue.hanzi: 因為我頭痛，所以在家睡覺。
dialogue.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ tóu tòng, suǒyǐ zài jiā shuìjiào.
dialogue.gloss: Because I had a headache, so I slept at home.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 那這個週末呢？如果天氣好，我們一起去騎腳踏車。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà zhège zhōumò ne? Rúguǒ tiānqì hǎo, wǒmen yìqǐ qù qí jiǎotàchē.
dialogue.gloss: What about this weekend? If the weather's good, let's go bike riding together.

dialogue.speaker: 阿明
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊！雖然我騎得不快，可是我很想去。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a! Suīrán wǒ qí de bú kuài, kěshì wǒ hěn xiǎng qù.
dialogue.gloss: Sure! Although I don't ride fast, I really want to go.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.hanzi: 我們先去吃早餐，然後騎到學校那邊。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān qù chī zǎocān, ránhòu qí dào xuéxiào nà biān.
dialogue.gloss: We'll eat breakfast first, then ride over to the school area.

dialogue.speaker: 阿明
dialogue.hanzi: 好，那邊的珍珠奶茶很好喝，而且不貴喔！
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo, nà biān de zhēnzhū nǎichá hěn hǎohē, érqiě bú guì o!
dialogue.gloss: OK, the bubble tea over there is really good, and it's cheap too!

sentences.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒ jiù bú qù le.
sentences.gloss: If it rains tomorrow, I won't go.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng suīrán xiǎo, dànshì cài hěn hǎochī.
sentences.gloss: Although this restaurant is small, the food is delicious.

sentences.pinyin: Tā wèile kǎoshì, zhōumò méi qù wán.
sentences.gloss: For the exam, she didn't go out to play on the weekend.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chī zǎocān, ránhòu qù shàngbān.
sentences.gloss: I eat breakfast first, then go to work.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfú hěn piàoliàng, érqiě bú guì.
sentences.gloss: This piece of clothing is pretty, and it's not expensive either.

passage.title: 週末的早餐
passage.hanzi: 週末的早上，我先搭捷運到台北車站，然後在附近的一家小店吃早餐。那家店雖然不大，可是東西很好吃，而且很便宜。老闆問我為什麼每個週末都來，我說：「為了你們的熱珍珠奶茶啊！」如果下次你也有時間，我們一起來。
passage.gloss: On weekend mornings I first take the MRT to Taipei Main Station, then eat breakfast at a little shop nearby. Although that shop isn't big, the food is delicious and very cheap. The owner asked me why I come every weekend, and I said, "For your hot bubble tea!" If you have time next time, let's come together.
